Seattle football · Since 1976

Seattle Seahawks History & The 12s

A sourced guide to the franchise timeline, championship eras, defining players, iconic numbers and the fan culture that shaped Seattle football.

Start at the beginning ↓

Built by fans, not the franchise. This is an independent, celebratory guide—not an official team history. Every timeline item links to its source.

From expansion team to two-time champion

The Seattle timeline

Playoff milestones are grouped with their NFL season, which can end in the following calendar year.

  1. 1974
    Beginnings

    Seattle is awarded an NFL franchise

    The NFL granted Seattle its expansion franchise on June 4, setting the stage for the club to begin play in 1976.

    Source: Pro Football Hall of Fame (opens in a new tab) ↗
  2. 1976
    Kingdome era

    Football arrives at the Kingdome

    The expansion Seahawks played their first season in the NFC, with Jim Zorn and Steve Largent beginning a partnership that helped define the early club.

    Source: HistoryLink (opens in a new tab) ↗
  3. 1983
    Kingdome era

    The first playoff run

    In Chuck Knox’s first season, Seattle beat Denver and Miami before its breakthrough postseason ended in the AFC Championship Game.

    Source: Pro Football Hall of Fame (opens in a new tab) ↗
  4. 1984
    The 12s

    No. 12 is retired for the fans

    Seattle retired the number 12 on December 15 as a tribute to the home crowd and its impact on games.

    Source: Seattle Seahawks (opens in a new tab) ↗
  5. 1989
    The 12s

    A Kingdome roar changes the rules

    The NFL briefly introduced an excessive-crowd-noise rule during an era when visiting offenses struggled to communicate inside the Kingdome.

    Source: Seattle Seahawks (opens in a new tab) ↗
  6. 1997
    Seattle football

    The franchise stays in the Northwest

    Paul Allen’s purchase secured the Seahawks’ future in the Pacific Northwest and cleared the way for a new stadium project.

    Source: Pro Football Hall of Fame (opens in a new tab) ↗
  7. 2002
    Lumen Field era

    A new outdoor home

    The Seahawks opened their new stadium, beginning the venue era that continues today at Lumen Field.

    Source: Lumen Field (opens in a new tab) ↗
  8. 2002
    Conference move

    Seattle returns to the NFC

    NFL realignment moved the Seahawks from the AFC West to the NFC West, the conference where they had played their inaugural season.

    Source: Pro Football Hall of Fame (opens in a new tab) ↗
  9. 2003
    The 12s

    The 12 Flag tradition begins

    Twelve original season-ticket holders raised the 12 Flag before the October 12 home game, launching a lasting pregame ritual.

    Source: Seattle Seahawks (opens in a new tab) ↗
  10. 2005
    Championship season

    The first NFC crown

    A 13–3 team powered by Shaun Alexander, Matt Hasselbeck and Walter Jones won the NFC and reached the franchise’s first Super Bowl.

    Source: Pro Football Hall of Fame (opens in a new tab) ↗
  11. 2010
    Iconic moment

    Beast Quake shakes Seattle

    Marshawn Lynch’s 67-yard playoff touchdown against New Orleans sent the stadium crowd into a celebration measured by a nearby seismic station.

    Source: Seattle Seahawks (opens in a new tab) ↗
  12. 2013
    Championship season

    Defense carries Seattle to the summit

    The top-seeded Seahawks capped a dominant season by winning Super Bowl XLVIII, the first league championship in franchise history.

    Source: Pro Football Hall of Fame (opens in a new tab) ↗
  13. 2014
    Championship season

    Back-to-back NFC champions

    Seattle returned to the Super Bowl after winning a second consecutive NFC championship.

    Source: Pro Football Hall of Fame (opens in a new tab) ↗
  14. 2025
    Championship season

    A second Lombardi Trophy

    A 14–3 regular season ended with Seattle defeating New England 29–13 in Super Bowl LX for the franchise’s second league championship.

    Source: Seattle Seahawks (opens in a new tab) ↗

Sounds, styles and turning points

Eras & identities

01

Kingdome beginnings

Jim Zorn’s improvisation and Steve Largent’s precision gave the expansion club its first personality. Chuck Knox’s hard-running teams then delivered Seattle’s first deep playoff run.

Source: Pro Football Hall of Fame ↗
02

Holmgren’s offense

Matt Hasselbeck, Shaun Alexander and a line anchored by Walter Jones powered the 2005 team to 13 wins and the franchise’s first NFC championship.

Source: Pro Football Hall of Fame ↗
03

Legion of Boom

The 2013 defense led the NFL in points allowed, yards allowed and takeaways, then overwhelmed Denver in Super Bowl XLVIII.

Source: Pro Football Hall of Fame ↗
04

A new champion

The 2025 Seahawks paired a 14–3 regular season with a defense that held New England scoreless for three quarters in Super Bowl LX.

Source: Seattle Seahawks ↗

How this page was built

Sources & method

Timeline claims are paraphrased from the linked source on each entry. We prioritize the Pro Football Hall of Fame, HistoryLink’s Washington history encyclopedia, Lumen Field, and team-published records. Numbers are included only when those sources state them directly. This page favors defining moments over completeness. Send corrections through the corrections process.
